name: Marrakech
tagline: Gardens, palaces and rooftops, with the Atlas on the horizon.
distinctive: The Medina's palaces and madrasas, Jardin Majorelle and the Yves Saint Laurent museum, the ritual of the hammam, and the High Atlas an hour away.

image.alt: The cobalt-blue villa and cacti of the Jardin Majorelle in Marrakech

moodNotes.city: Rooftop dinners, lamplit courtyards and the square at Jemaa el-Fnaa after dark.
moodNotes.art: The Bahia Palace, the Ben Youssef Madrasa, Jardin Majorelle and the Musée Yves Saint Laurent.
moodNotes.wellness: The hammam is a tradition here, and hotel gardens are made for doing nothing.
moodNotes.weekend: A short flight from much of Europe, and the airport is close to the city.
moodNotes.lifetime: A night in the Agafay desert or high in the Atlas makes the trip.

seasonNote: Spring and autumn are ideal. Summer is very hot, and winter nights are cold.

arrival.transfer: Menara Airport is close to the city. Transfers to the Medina or Hivernage typically take 15–25 minutes.
arrival.groundNote: Much of the Medina is closed to cars, so hotels arrange porters from the nearest drop-off point.

driving.note: The Medina is largely car-free. For the Atlas and the desert, a private driver who knows the roads is the better choice.

transfer.label: Private driver and 4×4
transfer.why: A driver for the Atlas valleys and the Agafay desert, where local knowledge matters more than horsepower.

stay.name: La Mamounia
stay.why: The celebrated palace hotel beside the old city walls, known for its large gardens and its Moorish and Art Deco interiors.

watchWhy: A square-cased classic from 1904, as considered as the zellige in a riad courtyard and at ease in the heat.
aromaWhy: Damask rose and orange blossom from the gardens, and Atlas cedar from the mountains.

days.title: Gardens
days.text: Visit Jardin Majorelle and the Musée Yves Saint Laurent in the morning. Book a hammam in the afternoon, then dine on a rooftop at sunset.

days.title: The Medina
days.text: See the Bahia Palace and the Ben Youssef Madrasa, then explore the souks with a good guide. Have dinner in a riad courtyard.

days.title: Into the Atlas
days.text: Take a driver into the Ourika valley or up to Imlil for lunch with mountain views, returning for the evening.

moreDays.title: A desert night
moreDays.text: Spend the night at a camp in the stony Agafay desert, less than an hour from the city.

moreDays.title: Essaouira
moreDays.text: Take a day or a night on the Atlantic, in a walled port town with a fine light and a breeze.
